regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: ER-positive early or advanced breast cancer
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Tamoxifen acts at oestrogen receptors. Its effects differ between tissues, which helps explain the distinct blood-clot and womb risks. It is not a cytotoxic chemotherapy infusion.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take tamoxifen once daily continuously. There is no planned week off. The prescriber confirms the duration for the treatment setting.
key_points: Adjuvant or advanced oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer in pre- or postmenopausal women, within the exact NCCP eligibility criteria.
20 mg orally once daily
History of significant thromboembolic disease is an NCCP exclusion. Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended. Interactions, including potent CYP2D6 inhibitors, need medication review.

For early breast cancer, discuss the initial endocrine course and a later decision about extending or changing treatment; some patients continue endocrine therapy to 10 years. Advanced treatment continues according to benefit and tolerance. A five-year review is not an automatic instruction to stop.

ECG is risk-based. For patients with QT risk, the cited tamoxifen product information recommends baseline ECG / electrolytes and repeat ECG after at least four weeks, with further checks as indicated. Routine echo surveillance is not required for tamoxifen alone.
Assess personal fracture and menopausal risks. Tamoxifen has a different effect on bone from aromatase inhibitors; do not automatically copy an AI bone-density schedule.

ATLAS: duration review after five years: Years 5–14 recurrence:21.4% versus 25.1%; breast-cancer mortality:12.2% versus 15.0%. Extended treatment increased pulmonary embolus risk (RR 1.87) and endometrial-cancer risk (3.1% versus 1.6% during years 5–14). A planned risk–benefit discussion, not automatic ten-year treatment for everyone. Benefit and harm populations differ: cancer efficacy is ER-positive, safety analyses include all receptor groups. Published correction is listed.

route_and_duration: Swallow the tablet whole, with or without food. If a dose is missed or vomited, do not replace it; take the next scheduled daily dose.

regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: After early breast cancer treatment, endocrine therapy reduces the risk of recurrence. In advanced disease, the aim is to control cancer and symptoms. Your setting determines the duration and follow-up.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: After menopause, much of the body’s oestrogen is made when aromatase converts other hormones in fat and other tissues. Blocking that enzyme lowers oestrogen signalling in hormone-sensitive breast cancer. It does not reliably switch off functioning ovaries: ovarian suppression, if needed, must be prescribed and checked separately.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take anastrozole once daily continuously. There is no planned week off. The treatment setting determines the intended duration.
key_points: Postmenopausal hormone-sensitive breast cancer in the NCCP adjuvant, switch-after-tamoxifen or advanced settings. The exact receptor and prior-treatment criteria remain a prescribing decision.
1 mg orally once daily
A functioning premenopausal ovarian state is not compatible with AI monotherapy. Severe hepatic impairment is not recommended by NCCP; moderate impairment requires caution.

In early breast cancer, the standard source course is five years of adjuvant endocrine treatment, including any planned switch from tamoxifen. A later extension decision depends on recurrence risk, tolerance and bone health. Advanced treatment continues according to benefit.
There is no routine ECG or echo schedule for anastrozole alone. Review cardiovascular risk factors and investigate cardiac symptoms when indicated.

Offer baseline DXA when starting an adjuvant aromatase inhibitor if not already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates; assess fracture risk and relevant previous results. Under the 2025 joint guidance, patients with a T-score above −2.0 and no additional risk factors generally have risk and bone density reassessed every one to two years. Patients on bone-protective treatment generally have BMD reassessed about every two years. Fracture, substantial bone loss or a change in risk can require earlier review. The clinician selects the interval and any bone treatment; these are not automatic yearly scans for everyone.

MA.17: extended adjuvant letrozole after tamoxifen: At 30 months median follow-up, DFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.76); distant DFS HR 0.60 (0.43–0.84). Overall OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.82,0.57–1.19). Stopped early for benefit. Supports a specific post-tamoxifen extension strategy, not indefinite treatment or automatic extension after every previous AI course.

P 024: neoadjuvant letrozole: Clinical response 55% versus 36%; breast-conserving surgery 45% versus 35%. Short preoperative response study, not a survival trial. Clinical reassessment and surgical planning remain essential; the trial duration must not override NCCP's individualized 4–8 month neoadjuvant window.
